resources.string: Show this tool on the toolbar and in the toolbox
Add the API key below to turn this tool on
Needs a SearXNG instance. Add its address under Search settings.
Voice typing is off. Turn it on under All voice typing settings below.
Add a source under Emoji › Emoji mixes first.
Set up a song recogniser with your key under Song recognisers below to turn this tool on
Make a secondary layout under Key layouts below to turn this tool on
Off keeps it out of the toolbox. It still works from the toolbar, by typing its name and from selection actions.
Keyboard height, width, alignment and split
Keyboard height, width, alignment and floating mode
Keyboard height, width, alignment and the keep-on-screen switch
Keyboard height, width, alignment and one-handed mode
How the app grid orders the apps
Show each app\'s name under its icon
Show the apps you opened last in a row above the grid
The keyboard keeps the last 10 apps you opened from this tool, on your device only. Turn this off to stop the tracking and delete the list.
List an app’s screens on its page
Press and hold an app and pick the last item in the menu to open its page. With this off the page keeps its pin, hide and App info actions and leaves the screens out.
Also list screens that only the app itself may open
Android does not let other apps open these screens. They show dimmed, and a press on one does nothing. Useful to explore what an app contains.
Turn plugins on, see which ones are installed, and see what each one can do
Suggestions, the history tab, the emoji row, skin tones and favourites
Your snippets, triggers, patterns and template variables
History, the panel, the paste chip, and what happens to a copied password
Turn the torch off when the keyboard closes

On: a torch you turned on from the keyboard goes off when the keyboard closes or when you change apps, so it is never left on in your pocket. A torch turned on from the quick settings tile or another app is left alone. Off: the torch stays on until you turn it off again, from the tool or from the quick settings tile of the system.
Show the heading in numbers under the compass rose
Mark the direction of the Kaaba on the compass

The keyboard computes the qibla bearing from the location that you save in the weather tool. The two tools share that location. The keyboard computes everything on your device, and the compass never uses the network.
No location is saved yet. Set one under Tools → Weather.
Show the pitch and the roll in degrees under the bubble
Both shortcuts are standard for redo. Which one works depends on the app that you type in. If redo does nothing, try the other one.
Show the moon the way it looks south of the equator
Show the name of each phase in Arabic as well, under the name in your language
Fetch the forecast as you type
Off, a weather chip waits for your tap before it goes online
This setting controls only the chip on the suggestion strip. The panel fetches the forecast when you open it. The F-Droid edition starts with this setting off.
The weather and the place search both use Open-Meteo, only when you use them. The keyboard makes no other network requests.
Its day number also shows inside each day cell
The keyboard shows it in the header and under the selected day
Move the computed Hijri date to match the local moon sighting

The tool uses the arithmetic (tabular) Hijri calendar. Real Islamic months start at the sighting of the crescent moon. That can differ from the tables by one or two days. Set the offset that matches your local authority.

Select any two calendars to show next to the Gregorian one. The keyboard computes Chinese dates from astronomy. The Hebrew, Persian, Hindu (Saka), Buddhist and Japanese calendars are exact arithmetic. Hijri is the tabular calendar, so it has the day offset above.\n\nAll three start from the region of your device: the Bengali calendar in Bangladesh, era years in Japan, a Friday and Saturday weekend across much of the Middle East. That is only a guess at what you want. You can change all of it here.

Press a day to see its events from the calendar of your device, and press an event to change it, delete it or type it into your text. The keyboard asks to read your calendar the first time that you open the tool, and to write to it the first time that you save an event.
Where Save puts a new event

In the keyboard writes the event straight into your calendar, and asks for calendar access the first time. In the calendar app opens your calendar app\'s own editor with the event filled in, and you save it there. Changing and deleting events always happens in the keyboard.
The calendar a new event starts in
Allow calendar access to choose one
How long a new event runs
The reminder a new event starts with
Open the tool on the front camera instead of the back one
Save front camera photos the way the preview shows them

Camera sensors record selfies without a mirror. The text then reads correctly, but the photo looks turned around next to the preview. On: the saved photo matches what you saw while you framed it. Off: the keyboard keeps the true orientation of the sensor.
Also keep photos in Pictures/WM Keyboard
This setting is off by default, because photos that you take here are normally one-time sends and not photos to keep. On: the keyboard copies every photo into the gallery and also sends it.

Search finds pages about what is in a photo: a plant, an insect, a landmark, a product. The image search tool has a camera button that always offers Search. The switch below adds Search to the camera tool too.
Add Search next to Retake and Send
Google Lens and the share sheet give the photo to another app, and the keyboard sends nothing itself. Web sends the photo to the search site that you pick and opens the results in your browser.
Opens Lens in the Google app. If the Google app is not installed, the share sheet opens.
Sends the photo to a search site and opens its results in your browser. No Google app necessary.
Lets you pick an app that searches with a photo, each time.

None of these sites has a public way to send photos. The keyboard does what the site\'s own upload button does, so a site can stop working when it changes. If that happens, pick a different site. Custom sends the photo to your own server.
The keyboard sends the photo here as form data. The server answers with a redirect to the results, or with the results address.
The form field that holds the photo
Keep the full 4:3 picture instead of the part in the viewfinder

The viewfinder is as wide as the keyboard, so the top and the bottom of the picture go off the screen. The keyboard usually cuts those parts away, and you send what you saw. On: you send the full 4:3 photo, which holds more than the viewfinder showed you. The preview does not change.
Play the camera click when you take a photo
Vibrate on the shutter, the controls and the timer countdown
This uses the haptic style and strength of the keyboard, under Typing → Feedback. If the keyboard haptics are off, the camera tool stays silent too.

The keyboard cuts photos down to what the viewfinder shows, saves them in the private storage of the app and sends them into the chat. Nothing goes into your gallery, and the camera runs only while the tool is open.\n\nTurn on “Send the whole photo” if you want the full 4:3 picture and not only the part in the viewfinder.
Look up the word at the cursor
The tool searches the selected word or the current word when it opens

Translations come from Wiktionary. When the word was found in Wiktionary, its translations come on the same page, so nothing more is sent. When another source found the word, the tool asks Wiktionary for the translations as well, but only if Wiktionary is on in the dictionary sources.
Show the word in other languages under its definitions. Tap a translation to type it
Your keyboard languages. Add a language other than English, or pick some here
The tool shows the translations that Wiktionary has for these languages, in this order. Pick none to follow your keyboard languages.
Definitions come from the sources below, in their order. The keyboard sends the word that you look up to an online source only when you use the tool.
Where the tool looks for definitions, in order

The tool asks the first source that is on. When that source does not know the word, or cannot be reached, the tool asks the next one. Drag a source to change the order, and turn off a source to never ask it. Online sources receive only the word you look up.

Yomichan and Yomitan dictionaries, in any language: Japanese with readings and pitch accent (JMdict, Jitendex), Chinese, Korean, and the Wiktionary dictionaries for many other languages. StarDict dictionaries work too, as plain text. Import the dictionary\'s zip or tar file. Inflected Japanese words find their dictionary form. The source list above asks them as one source, Imported dictionaries; inside it they answer in this order.
A Yomichan or Yomitan dictionary zip, or a StarDict dictionary in a zip or tar. A large one takes some minutes.

Whole English dictionaries kept on the phone, so the Dictionary tool can define ordinary words with no connection, and in the build without internet access. The vocabulary packs know only their own lists\' words. Once one is here, the source list above asks it wherever you put it; by default after the online sources, so it answers when they cannot be reached. Wiktionary, offline, is Wiktionary\'s common words with pronunciation (CC BY-SA 4.0). Open English WordNet has every single English word in WordNet, with shorter definitions (CC BY 4.0).
The file downloaded is not this dictionary. Try again later.
The server refused the download (HTTP %1$s). Try again later.
A .wmdict.gz file fetched on another device or in a browser
The packs the Vocabulary packs source reads, offline. They know only the words of their own lists, so most words need an online source
Pause between repeats while you hold an arrow or backspace. A lower value is faster
Hold to repeat on the toolbar
Holding this tool on the toolbar keeps moving the cursor. Off, holding it opens this page instead
One switch for all eight moving cursor tools. Dragging the tool from the toolbar still moves it.
Hold to repeat in the toolbox
Do the same in the toolbox grid. This tool only, and off by default
A hold in the toolbox is how you open a tool\'s page from the keyboard, so this tool gives that up while this is on. Its page stays under Tools. Turn it on only for the moves you actually hold.
Pause between moves while you hold the tool. A lower value is faster. Shared with the text editing tool
Selection mode stays on while you hold the tool. It stops when you let go, and the selected text stays selected
This spends the press and hold on the toolbar, so this page is where you change the tool, or a hold in the toolbox. To move the tool, press and hold it and then drag it, as before.
Two quick presses select the word at the cursor. Three select the full line

The first press of a pair still turns selection mode on or off, in the same way the shift key gives you caps lock. Turn this off if you press the tool twice in quick succession and want no word selected.
Where Word left and Word right stop, and what Select word takes

The same setting applies to Word left, Word right and Select word.\n\nPress Select word again to also select the word on each side. Press shift and then Select word to go back one step. If \"Shift changes the case of the selection\" is on, shift changes the case instead.
The app moves the cursor as it does for Ctrl and an arrow key. Most apps treat \"wmkeyboard.pages.dev\" as one word.
The cursor stops only at spaces. An address is one word.
The cursor also stops at a dot, a slash, an underscore or another mark, so it can stop at \"wmkeyboard.|\".

While selection mode is on, every cursor move selects text: the cursor tools, the text editing panel, the spacebar cursor swipe and the volume keys. Turn it off to keep what you selected and stop selecting more.
How far your finger travels for each character. A lower value moves the cursor faster
How far your finger travels for each line. A lower value moves the cursor faster
The trackpad stays open while you hold the tool and closes when you let go. A tap opens it until the next tap
This spends the press and hold on the toolbar, so this page is where you change the tool, or a hold in the toolbox. To move the tool, press and hold it and then drag it, as before.
Two quick taps on the trackpad select the word at the cursor. Three select the full line
A short tick for every character or line the cursor moves
Draw your finger\'s path and a crosshair on the trackpad while you drag
Show the text at the cursor, larger, above the cursor while you drag
The magnifier shows the line of text around the cursor. It goes above the cursor when the app tells the keyboard where the cursor is. If the app does not, it goes above the keyboard.
One finger moves the cursor. Hold, then drag to select. Two fingers move a word at a time, and a two-finger tap types a space.
7 8 9 on the top row, like a desk keypad. Off puts 1 2 3 on top, like a dialer
The keyboard learns no words and no emoji habits from your typing
Copies do not go into the history of the clipboard tool
Copy and cut from the keyboard do not go to the system clipboard, so other apps cannot read them

While incognito is on, text you copy or cut with the keyboard stays inside the keyboard. The paste keys of the keyboard paste it back. When incognito goes off, the keyboard forgets it.\n\nIf you have not copied with the keyboard yet, paste gives what is on the system clipboard, as usual. The copy and paste menu of the app itself still uses the system clipboard.
Offer this tool\'s answer on the suggestion strip. Set under Typing
The same switch that the toolbar tool uses

This drops the features below until you turn it off again. It stays on after a restart and at any battery level. A full battery does not turn it off.\n\nNothing is lost. The features come back exactly as you had them, because power saving never rewrites your settings. It only hides them while it is on.
As well as the switch above
Only the switch above turns power saving on
Follows the system switch, so the keyboard saves power when you asked your device to
Whichever of the two happens first
\"Android battery saver\" follows the system switch, so the keyboard saves power exactly when you already asked your device to. \"Battery is low\" uses your own percentage below instead.
Power saving starts at this level or below it
Ignore the automatic triggers while the charger is in
There is nothing to save while the battery fills, so the automatic triggers stop. This does not change the switch above. If you turn power saving on by hand, it stays on.
A bundle of the switches further down
Vibration, sounds, animations, the glide trail, glass blur and the background watchers
Light, plus background fetches and the on-device models
Balanced, plus glide typing, emoji suggestions and smart chips
Your own mix of the switches further down
Stop transitions and motion, as reduced motion does
Stop drawing the trail behind a swiped word
This drops only the trail. Glide typing still works. The keyboard draws the trail on every frame of a gesture, so it costs more than the decode that it decorates.
Stop the character bubble over each key
Stop glass themes blurring the app behind the keyboard and its popups
A swipe decode is the most expensive thing the keyboard does. It is also why many people use the keyboard, so this setting is off by default and only the trail is dropped.
Stop reading what you type for emoji to offer
Stop matching sums, conversions and tool keywords as you type
No link previews and no automatic look-ups

This stops the requests that happen without you asking: previews for copied links and for scanned QR codes, and the look-up of the dictionary when you select a word. Tools that you open yourself still work, such as translate, search and GIFs.
Stop watching for new screenshots to offer in the clipboard
Use the system recognizer for voice typing, and glide a word instead of writing it

Offline voice typing and handwriting both run a neural model on the processor, which is the most expensive work the keyboard does. Voice typing goes back to the system recognizer, and the letter swipe goes back to glide typing.
Stop putting the media tool on the toolbar while music plays
Stop counting your typing. Days spent saving power record nothing
Power saving is a view of your settings and never a rewrite of them. Everything that it turns off here comes back exactly as you had it the moment power saving ends.
The tool uses this same switch. You can also find it under Typing
Suggestions, autocorrect, capital letters and more
The tool uses this same switch. You can also find it under Advanced

Turns English words on and off for the phonetic layout you are typing on (Avro, Hindi phonetic). The setting itself is on each language\'s own screen, next to Also suggest from, and needs English picked there.
Type English words as English, and the switch on the suggestion strip
Where the bar appears, which actions it offers, and their order
The style the tool turns on. The strip over the keys still changes it
Select a style and the tool always starts there. The strip over the keys changes the style for the rest of the session, and your selection here stays as it is.
Keep the language after you turn it off
Fancy text stays in the language cycle of the 🌐 key
The tool adds Fancy text to your languages when you turn it on. With this setting off, the tool deletes it again when you turn it off, so the 🌐 key cycles only the languages you read.
Turn off when the keyboard closes
The next time you type, the keyboard is back in your own language
Fancy text is usually one name or one message. This setting takes the keyboard back to the language you came from as soon as you leave the field. It applies only when the tool turned Fancy text on.
The saved style, and the layout switch
The tool types with Unicode letters, not with a font. The letters stay fancy in every app, but a screen reader cannot read them and a search cannot find them.
The secondary layout the tool puts on screen, or a list to select from

With no layout selected here, the tool opens a list of all your secondary layouts, or the only one you have. Select a layout and the tool shows that one directly. A press while a secondary layout is on screen always takes it off again. A key on any layout can also open a secondary layout.
A secondary layout is a grid of your own, such as a symbols page or a macro pad. It is not a language. It keeps the dictionary of the layout you type with.
Haptic style and strength, key preview, press and hold
The haptic style and strength are under Key press → Haptic feedback. The panel of the tool changes the same settings from the keyboard.
Only an S Pen or another stylus draws. The keyboard ignores finger touches
This helps to reject the palm while you write with a stylus. Even with this setting off, the keyboard ignores finger touches for a short time after stylus strokes, so a resting palm does not draw.
Put a space between words that you write one after another
Offline recogniser for Chinese and Japanese
Read Chinese and Japanese with zinnia instead of Google ML Kit

zinnia is a small open-source recogniser with models from the Tegaki project. It reads one character at a time and is less accurate than ML Kit, but needs nothing from Google. Builds without ML Kit, such as the F-Droid one, always use it. Simplified or Traditional Chinese follows the Traditional characters switch in Chinese settings.
Reset it to follow the theme\'s accent
How the strokes leave the canvas
Open the canvas taller than the keyboard, without changing the keys
How long after the last stroke the keyboard waits before it recognizes the word
A shorter pause feels faster, but it can cut multi-stroke letters and Bengali conjuncts in half. A longer pause gives you more time between strokes. Gboard uses about half a second.
How the full-screen canvas tells your writing apart from taps on the app
Tap the expand button on the handwriting panel to write anywhere over the app. The keyboard shrinks to a small bar and the canvas is see-through, so you can watch the text arrive.
A pen button on the bar switches between writing and using the app. Works with a finger or any stylus
A stylus writes and a finger keeps using the app. Start each run of writing over a text field. Needs Android\'s own setting for writing in text fields with a stylus

One model for each language that you type in. Recognition runs fully on your device, with Google ML Kit, zinnia for Chinese and Japanese, or PaddleOCR where ML Kit has no model (one row per script). Each needs a one-time download, and its size is shown on its own row — they range from about 8 MB to about 52 MB. After that, handwriting works offline.
Add a language to get its handwriting model here
Install and choose the icons on the keys and tools
Choose which set the keyboard draws emoji with
Choose the font the keys are lettered in
Create, edit, import and export keyboard themes
Where the translation comes from. You can also change this on the panel.

Online sends the text to the translation service and knows the most languages. On device uses Google ML Kit models that you download, about 30 MB for each language: the text stays on the phone and it works with no connection. Automatic uses the device when the languages are downloaded and the online service for the rest. On-device translation is good for messages and short text, and less exact than the online service for long or technical text.
The language lists on the panel start with the languages on the device. With On device and Automatic.
With On device, the language lists on the panel show the downloaded languages, the languages you type in and the current selection. All languages, at the end of the list, shows the rest.

Each language is one download. A translation needs the models of the two languages, and goes through English when neither of them is English. The list starts with the language you translate into and the languages you type in.

Mozilla\'s models for the Bergamot engine, the same ones Firefox translates with. Each direction is its own download: French → English reads French, English → French writes it. A translation between two languages that are not English goes through English and needs both directions. The engine itself is a separate download of a few megabytes on builds that do not carry it. Needs a 64-bit phone with Android 9 or later.

Meta\'s NLLB-200, one model for 200 languages that translates between any two of them. It is the on-device engine for the pairs Firefox Translations and ML Kit have no model for. One download of 630 MB, plus its CTranslate2 engine of a few megabytes on builds that do not carry it. While Translate is open it takes about 1 GB of memory, and a sentence takes a few seconds. Needs a 64-bit phone with 6 GB of memory or more.

The NLLB-200 model (%1$s) downloads from Hugging Face under Meta\'s licence for it, Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0. You may use it for non-commercial purposes only, and its translations come with no warranty. Accept to download it.
On-device translation is an extra part of the keyboard that downloads when you first need it. Download it, then select the languages.
Downloading the on-device translation part: %1$s of %2$s
This offline build cannot translate on this phone: its one engine, Firefox Translations, needs a 64-bit phone with Android 9 or later. To translate, install the standard build.
This offline build translates on the phone only. Open On device (Firefox Translations) under Providers, then get its library and the language directions you want on another device, and import them.
The download did not finish. Check the connection, then try again.
The on-device translation part is a separate download.
Part of the engine. No download is necessary
Without a key, translation uses the free public endpoint of Google

The keyboard sends the text that you translate to Google either way, and only while the translate panel is open. The free endpoint is unofficial and rate limited. A Cloud Translation key makes it official and reliable. If you set up DeepL below, DeepL gets the text instead, and Google gets only the languages that DeepL does not have.

Optional. For a server that you run, or a service that you pay for, that answers OpenAI chat completion requests: llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI and others. With an address here, the Online engine sends all translations to this server, and to no other service, even when the server fails. On Automatic, the translations that do not happen on the device go to it. The keyboard asks the model to translate and sends the text.
For example http://192.168.1.10:8080/v1. Keep empty to use the usual service.
The name of the model on the server. Keep empty if the server has only one model.
Only for a server that asks for a key

DeepL is optional. Nothing changes until you add a DeepL API key or a server address. Get a key in your DeepL account. The Free plan includes 500,000 characters each month. The keyboard sends text to DeepL only when you translate or when you tap DeepL Write.
Free keys end in :fx. The keyboard picks the correct DeepL server for your key.
For a proxy that you run. Keep empty to use the DeepL servers.
The online engine uses DeepL. Languages that DeepL does not have use the usual service.
Adds a DeepL Write button to the grammar panel and a DeepL Write action to the selection actions
DeepL Write corrects and rewrites text in the same language. It works with a DeepL API Pro key only. A Free key gets an error.
How DeepL Write rewrites your text. Languages without styles ignore it.
Make, edit, import and export your own packs
Offer your stickers as you type
In a chat, type the title of a sticker, one of its keywords or one of its emoji to see it

Only your own stickers, from your sticker packs. A sticker shows when the text before the cursor ends with its full title, with one of its keywords, or with one of its emoji. Set the title and the keywords when you edit a sticker in its pack. The keyboard does this only in fields that can receive images, so it never offers a sticker that the app cannot take. It also works in the emoji panel: pick an emoji that one of your stickers has and the sticker shows above the panel. Nothing leaves the phone to find them.
A row of large stickers at the top of the keyboard. The word suggestions stay where they are. Move the row in Rows and bars
Three small stickers on the suggestion strip, next to the words. A button shows the rest
A small chip on the strip that says how many stickers there are. Tap it to see them
The sticker replaces the title, keyword or emoji that you typed
The sticker is sent and your text stays in the field
Hold a sticker in the tray to see it large, and slide to see the others
Hide the toolbar and move the search up next to a back button

The GIF and sticker panels take the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row step aside, and the search box moves into the row that they leave. The grid then gets every pixel. This applies to both tools.
The most GIFs side by side. Fewer makes each one bigger
The most stickers side by side. Fewer makes each one bigger

Each picture keeps its shape, so a wide one takes more of its row than a square one, and a row of wide ones can hold fewer than this. To see more rows at one time, make the panel taller with Panel height, or drag the bar on top of the panel.
The space around each GIF and sticker in the grid. This applies to both tools
Open the panel on the search you left it on, instead of trending

On, closing the panel or moving to another text box keeps the search and the category chip you picked, and the panel opens on them next time. Off, the panel always opens on trending with no search typed. This applies to both tools.
Hide the search when you scroll
Scroll down to fold the search box and the chips away, and scroll up to bring them back
Long-press a GIF and choose Add to favourites. A Favourites chip then leads the category chips. Long-press it again to remove it.
Show a Recent chip with the GIFs you sent last
The list keeps the last 48 GIFs and stays on the phone. Incognito does not add to it. Turn this off to delete the list.
Save a copy of each favourite, so it shows and sends without a connection
The copies download when you add a favourite or open Favourites, and only on a connection that data saving allows. Turn this off to delete the copies. Your favourites stay.

The results get the room that the search box, the source chips and the category chips take. When you are at the top of the results, pull down to bring them back. While you type a search, the search box always shows. This applies to both tools.
Free from partner.klipy.com. The Tenor API closed in the middle of 2026
Search the Internet Archive\'s GeoCities GIFs too. No key needed

GifCities holds the GIFs the Internet Archive saved from GeoCities home pages before 2009: under construction signs, spinning globes, small animated clip art. Your search goes to gifcities.archive.org and the GIFs load from web.archive.org. These GIFs have no content rating, so the content filter does not apply to them. GIFs only, never stickers.
The GIF and sticker tools share all of this, and the content filter below. Any one key is enough. Every source that has a key shows up in the panel.
What the sticker tool gives to the chat app
Stickers arrive as real stickers in WhatsApp. Other apps get a plain image
Always a plain image, which every app accepts

Android has no sticker mark. The only signal is the MIME type of the file, and the receiving app decides. Sticker: the keyboard offers the WhatsApp sticker type first, so stickers arrive as real stickers there. Apps that do not support it get a normal image. Image: the keyboard always sends a plain image.
Images by default, because most chat apps animate them
Always a plain image, which every app animates
Only for GIFs that arrive in WebP form. The rest still go out as images

Sticker mode works only for GIFs that the source gives in WebP form. Android ships no encoder for animated WebP, so the keyboard cannot turn a real animated GIF into a sticker. Those GIFs always go out as images.
One chip for each source on the panel
One grid, with the results from every source mixed evenly
Hides only the strongest results. The PG-13 rating
Suitable for most chats. The PG rating
Hides the most. The G rating
KLIPY and GIPHY give each result a rating. Each service applies your level to its own results.
How many items one search or the trending view loads. Your own sticker packs always show fully.
From api-dashboard.search.brave.com, with a free monthly credit

Web search and image search share everything here. They search the whole web. The Brave plan includes a free monthly credit of about a thousand searches. Brave asks for attribution, so the panel shows \"via Brave\".
From app.tavily.com, with 1,000 free credits a month

Another search service, made for AI tools. The free plan gives 1,000 credits a month, and each search uses one. With a key here, web search and image search use Tavily instead of Brave. Image search shows the pictures that Tavily found on the pages of its results, so it finds fewer pictures than Brave.
Each search uses one API request either way

The online readers, in order. A vision model reads the photo at an address you choose and writes out the text it sees: any service with an OpenAI-compatible API works, such as OpenAI, OpenRouter, Gemini, Mistral, or Ollama or LM Studio on your own computer. A Rens server is a free front end to Google Lens. Both read any script and need no language data. Each scan sends the photo to the reader that is asked, and a paid service may charge for it.

Add a Rens server here to get a Translate button after you take a photo. The photo comes back with its text translated into the language that the Translate tool translates into. You can then send it, or retake it. The photo goes to the server you add, and from there to Google Lens.
Show the answer from the search engine
A short answer above the results, when the engine writes one

Tavily writes a short answer to your query from the pages it found, and some SearXNG instances give instant answers. With this on, that answer shows in a box above the results, with buttons to copy it or put it in your text. Brave gives no answer with a normal search key, so nothing shows when Brave does the search. On Tavily the answer costs no extra credits.
What a tap on a result does. Press and hold one for the menu
Open in the browser, insert the link or copy it, and for a picture send it or save it to the gallery.
Puts the link in your text, or the picture itself. The button beside a web result opens it.
Opens the page, or the page a picture is on. The button beside a web result inserts its link.
Faster answers, or better results for more credits

Tavily has four search depths. Basic is the default. Ultra fast and Fast answer sooner and cost 1 credit, but they do not take SafeSearch, so results are not filtered at those depths. Advanced looks deeper into each page for the parts that match your query, and costs 2 credits. The free plan gives 1,000 credits each month.
Show these beside All and Images in the search panel
Your instance did not list its categories, so these are the usual ones

SearXNG sorts its search engines into categories, such as news, videos, science and music. The ones you pick here show as chips in the search panel, beside All and Images, and a tap on one searches in that category only. The list comes from your instance, so it shows only the categories that the instance has. Images is always a tab of its own. The chips show only while a SearXNG instance does the search.
The quickest answer, with one short summary of each page. 1 credit. No SafeSearch.
Quicker than Basic, with results nearly as good. 1 credit. No SafeSearch.
The balance of speed and good results. 1 credit.
The best results, a little slower. 2 credits.
Deselect words to cut the capture down. Off starts empty, and you select the words one by one
Recognition runs on your device. No photo and no text leaves your device, and it works offline. After a capture, press words to select exactly what the keyboard types or copies.

ML Kit reads Latin script text, for example English or French, and on a phone with Google Play services also Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Devanagari. Tesseract reads more than 100 languages in most scripts, for example Bangla, Arabic, Russian and Chinese, but each language needs a one-time download. Automatic reads with ML Kit what it can, Chinese and Japanese with PaddleOCR where ML Kit cannot, and every other script with Tesseract.
Automatic reads Chinese, Japanese and Latin-script text, for example English or French, with PaddleOCR on your device, after a one-time download of 21 MB. Other scripts read only with Online model.

Tesseract reads a language only after the data for that language is on your device. There is one download for each language that you type in, from 0.4 MB to 12 MB. The data comes from the tessdata_fast set of the Tesseract project on GitHub. With Automatic, Chinese and Japanese share one download of 11 MB instead: the PP-OCRv5 models of PaddleOCR, which read them much better. You can also download a language from the scanner itself.

PaddleOCR reads only after its data is on your device: one download of 21 MB for every language it reads, the PP-OCRv5 models of the PaddleOCR project. You can also download it from the scanner itself.
None of the languages you turned on has Tesseract data. Add a language on the Languages screen. Its data then shows here.
Type the text of the code as soon as the keyboard finds one, with no confirm press
A short buzz when the keyboard finds a code
When a code is a web link, get the page title and description and show them above it. This needs an internet connection

Decoding runs on your device with ML Kit. It works offline and uploads nothing. It reads QR codes and the common product barcode formats, such as EAN, UPC and Code 128. Insert types the text of the code at the cursor. A link also gets an Open button.

Decoding runs on your device with zxing-cpp, without Google services. It works offline and uploads nothing. It reads QR codes, Data Matrix, Aztec, PDF417 and the product and industrial barcodes, such as EAN, UPC and Code 128. Insert types the text of the code at the cursor. A link also gets an Open button.
Use the open-source reader instead of ML Kit. It is a separate download of about 1 MB
Also keep scanned pages in Pictures/WM Keyboard

This opens the document scanner of Google, which is part of Google Play services, with edge detection, crop and shadow cleanup. Turn on the built-in scanner below to use the keyboard\'s own instead. Scanned pages come back as images. The keyboard puts them into the chat like a camera photo when it opens again. The processing runs on your device.

This opens the keyboard\'s own document scanner. It finds the page in the camera picture or a photo, lets you move its corners, flattens it, and can clean it up to white paper in colour, grey or black and white. Scanned pages come back as images. The keyboard puts them into the chat like a camera photo when it opens again. Everything runs on your device, without Google Play services.
Scan with the keyboard\'s own scanner instead of Google\'s
The built-in scanner is an extra part of the keyboard, about 2.5 MB. It downloads the first time you scan, or now.
The built-in scanner is a separate download of about 2.5 MB.
The recognition engine, the microphone view, spoken punctuation and the offline models
The spelling and style rules to check against
Pause after you stop typing before the issues refresh. A lower value feels faster, a higher value does less work
Show or hide this kind of issue in the grammar panel

Plain mistakes: a misspelling, a verb that disagrees with its subject, a missing comma, a word swapped for one that sounds like it. Leave these on unless something here is noisy for the way you write.
Writing that is correct but harder work to read than it needs to be: long sentences, a word repeated, a phrase that says the same thing twice.
Suggestions rather than fixes, offering a stronger way to say the same thing. Turn the group off if you would rather only hear about mistakes.
How the writing reads for its audience: spacing and formatting, a form that is standard in one region but not another, an informal turn of phrase.
Set WM Keyboard as the spell checker of Android
Mark the spelling mistakes but offer no corrections

Who checks your writing, in order. A check goes to the first checker that is on and knows the language you are typing in, and to the next one when that one cannot answer.

Harper runs on the phone, works offline, and checks English only. Nothing you type leaves the phone with it.

LanguageTool checks more than 30 languages, but it runs on a server, so the text in the field is sent there each time it is checked: to api.languagetool.org, LanguageTool's public server, unless you enter the address of a server you run yourself. It is off until you switch it on. It is never sent a password field or text typed in incognito. The public server takes 20 checks a minute, so a long note is checked a piece at a time.

Harper, the grammar engine built into the keyboard, can also act as the system spell checker of Android. It runs on your device, works offline and uploads nothing that you type, whatever the Checkers list above says. The underlines and correction menus inside other apps then come from it as well. The button above opens the system Spell checker screen. Select WM Keyboard there. It follows the dialect that you select above. If your device hides that screen, the button opens the input method settings instead.
Subdomain code: en, bn, de, fr, es …
Insert links as [Title](url) instead of the plain address
The searches and the article text come from the free APIs of wikipedia.org, only while you use the tool.
Symbols, with a space between each
Fractions, math operators, Greek letters, arrows, currency signs, superscripts, subscripts and typographic marks. Everything types on your device, like a normal key.
Trigonometry functions use degrees. Off uses radians
1 2 3 on the top row, like a dialer and the numpad. Off puts 7 8 9 on top, like a desk calculator
Maximum number of decimal places. The unit converter uses it too
Show a length in feet as feet and inches, not as a decimal

1 metre reads as \"3 ft 3.37 in\" instead of \"3.2808399 ft\". The chip writes the units the way that you did: \"1m\" answers with \"3 ft 3.37 in\" and \"1 meter\" answers with \"3 feet 3.37 inches\". Where there is no room for either, it falls back to \"3\'3\"\". Turn this off for the plain decimal.

There are 14 categories: length, mass, temperature, area, volume, speed, time, data, energy, power, pressure, angle, frequency and fuel economy. All conversions run on your device. The result precision follows the calculator setting. The panel opens again on the category and the units that you used last.
Rounding of the converted amount. Coins have their own setting
How a currency chip names the currency that it converted into

Name writes \"96.04 Rupee\", Symbol writes \"₹96.04\" and Code writes \"96.04 INR\". A currency with no symbol of its own falls back to its code. Coins keep their ticker, such as BTC, with every choice.
How long a fetched exchange rate stays fresh
The upstream rates update about one time each day. A value below 24 hours mostly changes how soon the keyboard tries a failed fetch again.
Off, a currency chip waits for your tap before it goes online

This setting controls only the chip on the suggestion strip. The panel fetches rates when you open it, and rates that the keyboard already has convert with no fetch. The F-Droid edition starts with this setting off.
Rates come from the source that you select in Currency rates from. None of the sources needs an API key. The keyboard remembers the from and to pair that you select on the panel.
Read amounts like \"1 btc\" and show coins in the converter

\"1 btc\", \"0.5 ETH\", \"2 bitcoin\" and \"100000 sats\" put the amount in your currency on the suggestion strip. Tickers that are also ordinary words, such as DOT, LINK and NEAR, only count when you type them in capitals. Coin prices are fetched only when you type a coin amount or select a coin on the panel.
Automatic keeps five meaningful digits, which fits both a whole coin and a fraction of one
Coin prices move much faster than the daily currency table
%1$d on. Select the coins that the keyboard reads and offers
Any ticker that your coin source quotes works. A ticker the source does not carry simply never converts.
Where the fiat exchange rates are fetched
Where the coin prices are fetched
Fall back to the remaining sources when the first one fails
Coin prices come from the source that you select in Coin prices from. None of the sources needs an API key. Prices are indicative and are not advice to buy or sell anything.
Side length of the PNG that the keyboard inserts
QR codes go out as images by default
Always a plain image, which every app accepts
Offers the WhatsApp sticker type, where the app supports it

Some chat apps draw a plain incoming image with no bubble. That can look like a sticker, even though it was sent as an image. Sticker mode offers the WhatsApp sticker type instead, where the app supports it.
Also keep generated codes in Pictures/WM Keyboard
Repairs about 7% of a damaged code. Holds the most text
Repairs about 15%. Good for a code on a screen
Repairs about 25%. Good for a code that you print
Repairs about 30%. Holds the least text
The keyboard generates the code on your device and follows what the text field contains.
Between words, for example - or . Leave it blank for none
The keyboard adds it to a random word
Skip PINs like 1111, 1234, 1212 and dates, which many apps refuse and guessers try first
The keyboard generates everything on your device with a cryptographic random source. It never stores it and never logs it. Passphrase words come from the bundled English word list of the keyboard.
The panel changes these as you use it, so they are also how it opens next time.
How many copies the panel opens on
Copies in a row, the last letter stretched, or a staircase
Nothing, a space, a new line, a comma, or your own
The panel stops at the last whole copy that fits and says so
What Insert does with the copies you had already typed
The copies you typed go, and the whole count takes their place, so the text ends with exactly that many.
The copies you typed stay, and the count is added after them.
Type the same thing this many times in a row and the strip offers the tool
The panel offers the last ten texts you repeated
Kept on this phone only, and never in a backup. Nothing is remembered in incognito mode, in password fields, or in fields that ask not to be learnt from.
Setups for each app and each field, and what each one changes
How many images sit side by side on the Images tab
This button opens the Images tab of web search, and shares its settings

Fewer columns means larger previews, which is easier to judge before you send one. More columns fits more results without scrolling. GIF results are not affected: they are laid out in justified rows so each one keeps its own shape. This setting is 3 by default.
Length of the recent apps row
A number that divides by the apps per row of your grid fills whole rows and leaves no gap at the end.
How many apps sit side by side in the grid
Auto fits as many apps as the keyboard width holds, three to six on most phones. Set a number to get larger targets or more apps on the screen. If the icons do not fit in a row, they become smaller.
How large each app icon is in the grid
With apps per row on Auto, larger icons also make each cell wider, so fewer apps fit in a row. The pinned and recent row keeps its own size.
The outline of each app icon
As on the phone shows each icon with the shape your home screen gives it. Old apps without an adaptive icon keep their own outline.
No apps are hidden. Press and hold an app in the panel, open its page from the menu, then tap the eye.

resources.string: What a tap on an app does

A press and hold on an app offers all three whatever you pick here. Split screen puts the app beside the one you are typing in and needs Android 12L or later, or the split screen helper. A floating window needs a device with a desktop or freeform window mode, such as many tablets; elsewhere the app opens full screen.

A press and hold on an app offers both whatever you pick here. A floating window needs a device with a desktop or freeform window mode, such as many tablets; elsewhere the app opens full screen. Split screen needs Android 12L or later, or the split screen helper.
Off. Turn on if split screen opens apps full screen
On. Split screen goes through Android\'s split screen switch
Two apps that open side by side with one tap
Also list the apps in your work profile
Work apps carry a briefcase on their icon. While work apps are paused they show dimmed, and opening one asks Android to turn work apps back on. The keyboard needs no extra permission for this.
No folders yet. Press and hold an app in the panel and pick Add to folder.

resources.string: The timer the camera opens on

The camera panel has a timer button that steps through off, 3 seconds and 10 seconds. This is where it starts each time you open the panel, so if you always use the same one you do not have to set it again.
Time before the tool fetches the weather again

The tool reuses the last reading for this long instead of asking the service again, which saves data and battery. Set it shorter if you are watching weather that is changing, longer if you only glance at it. Opening the tool after this time has passed fetches fresh numbers.
Longest edge of the photos you take
The smallest file, and the fastest to send
A good size for a photo in a chat
Enough detail to read a page of text
The most detail, and the biggest file

Larger photos hold more detail, which matters for a picture of a document somebody has to read. They also take longer to capture and to send, and use more data. The camera picks the closest size its sensor offers.
How much text the code may hold

A QR code holds more text at a lower error correction level, and less at a higher one. Raise this to fit a longer link or note; if the code then refuses to build, lower the error correction above, or shorten the text.
How many outgoing links the Links tab lists
A long article can have hundreds of links. The tool asks for this many and a longer list is cut short. 500 is as many as Wikipedia will return at once.
Leave empty for the usual set

Some sites accept only a few punctuation marks. Type the ones that site allows and the generator draws from those, so you do not have to generate again and again until a password comes out clean. Leave it empty to use the full set.
Press and hold on the toolbar
Do a second thing with this tool. Toolbar only: in the toolbox, press and hold always opens a tool\'s settings.
Press and hold repeats the move, so it cannot do a second action
Press and hold turns selection mode on, so it cannot do a second action
Press and hold opens the trackpad, so it cannot do a second action
Press and hold picks a voice typing mode, so it cannot do a second action. Turn that off under Voice typing to bind one.
Rename, recolour or remove the tags on your notes
Save to notes from other apps
An entry in the share sheet

Share text from any app and choose Save to notes, and it becomes a note. Share a link, a page from the browser say, and the note gets the page\'s title and its text with the layout taken off, under the link and tagged Read later, so the Read back tool can read it to you. A page that cannot be read is saved as the link alone. Works with the keyboard closed.
Notes you deleted, until they are gone for good
Show headings, lists and checklists formatted in the keyboard and in previews. Off, every note is plain text.
What you see when you tap the tool
How the list of notes is laid out in the keyboard
Shelf: pinned notes as wide cards, the rest in a grid
Timeline: one row per note, grouped by day
Save as note from a selection
What the selection bar\'s Save as note does
Make a new note each time
Add to the note I edited last
Every note, every tag and the trash
Delete every note? This cannot be undone. A backup that holds the Notes section can bring them back.
Offer your last ten searches when the Find field is empty. Never kept in incognito or from a password field
Put the media tool on the toolbar on its own while a music app is playing

The pin is temporary. It goes on the end of the toolbar, it never moves the tools you pinned yourself, and it disappears when the player does. If you have already pinned the media tool, nothing changes.
Which apps count as music. %1$d chosen
Granted. The media tool can read and steer what is playing
Needed before the keyboard can see what is playing. Tap to grant

Android only lets an app read other apps\' playback through a notification listener. The listener WM Keyboard registers reads no notifications at all. It exists so the media tool can find the session it steers.
Download a word list to start
Flashcards for what is due today
When you type a plain word that a pack has a stronger alternative for, a chip on the suggestion strip offers it: “hate → abhor”. Tap it for the word’s card, hold it to swap the word.
A chip when a plainer word could be one from your packs
Typing a pack word offers its card
How much plainer the typed word has to be
Where each part of a word card is shown: in the keyboard panel and the app, in the app only, or nowhere.
Opens its card, or types it
Looks it up in the Dictionary tool
Translations come from Wiktionary and are downloaded per pack and language, on their own once you pick them here or add a keyboard language.
Wiktionary’s recordings are fetched over the network; on mobile data they follow Data saver. Speech synthesis works offline and is the fallback.
Recording when there is one, else synthesised
Review in the keyboard panel or on the Review screen. Both use the same schedule.
Five boxes with gaps of 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days. A right answer moves a card up a box, a wrong one back to the first.
The SuperMemo rule Anki uses: each card has an ease that good answers raise, and gaps that grow with it.
Added to a review session on top of what is due
One word a day, drawn from your packs
Offered on the suggestion strip until you tap or dismiss it
The same word for everyone with your packs, in that span
How many text fields may offer the same word before it stops; dismissing it stops it at once
This edition translates with LibreTranslate, which is free software you can run yourself. Enter the address of an instance you trust.

GIFs come from Wikimedia Commons, whose collection is largely educational rather than reactive. Leave this empty for Commons, or point it at another MediaWiki.
